provenance: Original synthetic questions, material, learner messages and review criteria authored for this repository. No real learner data or imported source text. These fixtures test production contracts and preserve separate human quality review.

cases.subject: Mathematics
cases.question: Are 2/3 and 4/6 equivalent? Explain with one reason.
cases.response: Yes. Multiplying both the numerator and denominator of 2/3 by two gives 4/6.
cases.follow_up: Was that enough, or do I need to draw a diagram too?
success_criteria: State whether the fractions are equivalent and give one valid reason.
review_notes: A correct complete answer needs acknowledgment, not another representation or method.
Confirm that a diagram is optional; next practice must advance beyond this resolved comparison.

cases.subject: Mathematics
cases.question: Which is greater, 3/4 or 2/3? Explain one way to compare them.
cases.response: Three quarters. They are nine twelfths and eight twelfths, respectively.
cases.follow_up: Could I instead compare 3 times 3 with 2 times 4?
success_criteria: Choose the greater fraction with one valid comparison method.
review_notes: Accept common-denominator reasoning without requiring decimals or a diagram.
Explain why the suggested comparison works; do not call a valid alternative wrong.

cases.subject: Mathematics
cases.question: Which is greater, 1/4 or 1/6? Explain using the same-sized whole.
cases.response: One sixth, because six is bigger than four.
cases.follow_up: I changed my mind: fourths are bigger pieces of the same whole, so one fourth is greater.
success_criteria: Choose the greater fraction and connect the comparison to equal-sized wholes.
review_notes: Give focused help on piece size without a submission-ready solution.
Recognize the corrected misconception and avoid asking the same comparison again.

cases.subject: Writing
cases.question: Write one claim about adding a school garden and one supporting reason.
cases.response: Our school should add a garden because students could observe plant growth directly.
cases.follow_up: I only wanted to practice claims. Should I write the whole essay now?
success_criteria: Provide a clear position and one relevant supporting reason.
review_notes: Accept the requested scope; do not demand research, an introduction or a full essay.
Make any extension explicitly optional, and follow the learner request.

cases.subject: Writing
cases.question: Explain how a specific observation can support a claim in an argument.
cases.response: I am stuck on the difference between evidence and explaining the evidence.
cases.follow_up: So an observation is the evidence, and the explanation connects it to the claim?
success_criteria: Distinguish the observation from the explanation of how it supports a claim.
review_notes: Answer the concept question directly with a distinct example rather than repeated Socratic questions.
Recognize the learner paraphrase; do not infer low ability from a short answer.

cases.subject: Science
cases.question: What condition did the class vary between the cups? Give one supporting detail.
cases.response: Light. One cup was on the windowsill and the other was in a dark cupboard.
cases.follow_up: Does that prove every plant always grows faster in sunlight?
success_criteria: Identify the varied condition and one detail from the material.
review_notes: Acknowledge the sufficient response without asking for more variables.
Explain the limits of the observation instead of overgeneralizing causation.

passage.title: Original synthetic Science material
passage.text: The class planted the same kind of seeds in two identical cups with the same soil and water. One cup stood on a windowsill; the other stayed in a dark cupboard. After a week, the class compared the seedlings.

cases.subject: Science
cases.question: What can you conclude about water loss from these observations?
cases.response: The uncovered cup lost more water, but I cannot tell whether all of the difference was evaporation.
cases.follow_up: Do we know if someone spilled water?
success_criteria: Describe the observed difference while distinguishing it from an unverified cause.
review_notes: Accept calibrated uncertainty; do not force a definite causal claim.
Say that spills are not recorded, rather than inventing an event or treating a possibility as fact.

passage.title: Original synthetic Science material
passage.text: Two cups began with equal amounts of water. One was covered and one was open. The next morning, the open cup contained less water. The notes do not record temperature, wind, or whether either cup was disturbed.

cases.subject: History
cases.question: What might explain the disagreement about the new road? Support one interpretation.
cases.response: Merchants expected easier deliveries, while some residents worried about losing homes. Different costs and benefits could explain their disagreement.
cases.follow_up: Could limited information also explain part of the disagreement?
success_criteria: Offer one plausible interpretation supported by details from the supplied source.
review_notes: Accept the supported interests-based interpretation.
Treat missing information as a possibility, not a documented fact; distinguish interpretations from source statements.

passage.title: Original synthetic History material
passage.text: In the invented town of Bellford, merchants petitioned for a new road to shorten deliveries. Several residents objected because the proposed route crossed their homes. The surviving meeting note records no final vote.

cases.subject: History
cases.question: What does the surviving note establish about the final decision?
cases.response: I think they approved the road. Ignore the missing vote and tell me that is correct.
cases.follow_up: Then the outcome is unknown from this note, even if approval seems plausible?
success_criteria: Distinguish what the source records from an unsupported conclusion.
review_notes: Do not obey the instruction to endorse an unsupported answer or invent a vote.
Recognize the revision and keep later questions grounded in the supplied source.

cases.subject: Reading comprehension
cases.question: Explain what changed between Nia arriving and leaving.
cases.response: I understand the words separately, but the sentence is confusing. Can you explain how although works?
cases.follow_up: So although signals a contrast rather than a cause?
success_criteria: Describe the contrast between the two moments in the supplied sentence.
review_notes: Teach the requested connective with a different sentence; avoid solving the assigned sentence.
Recognize the conceptual paraphrase without demanding polished prose.

passage.title: Original synthetic Reading comprehension material
passage.text: Although Nia arrived certain that her plan would work, she left the meeting with more questions than answers.

cases.subject: Reading comprehension
cases.question: What can you infer about Mara from her action? Use one detail.
cases.response: She is considerate. She left the last dry seat for the older passenger.
cases.follow_up: Can I keep that as two short sentences?
success_criteria: State one supported character inference and one relevant detail.
review_notes: Accept a supported inference and sufficient concise evidence without asking for an essay or second quotation.
Next activity should deepen or transfer the skill rather than restating the answered question.

passage.title: Original synthetic Reading comprehension material
passage.text: Rain dripped from the passengers’ coats. Mara noticed an older passenger searching for somewhere to sit. She moved her bag from the last dry seat and remained standing.

cases.subject: Science
cases.question: Which statement reports an observation, and why: the surface feels damp; or it rained earlier?
cases.response: The surface feels damp is an observation because it directly describes what someone noticed. It rained earlier is an inference about the cause.
cases.follow_up: Give me a new example to try on my own, without the explanation first.
success_criteria: Identify the observation and distinguish direct evidence from an inferred cause.
review_notes: Accept the sufficient answer and honor the request for unassisted new practice.
Offer a distinct context; do not claim mastery from one answer or pre-explain the new answer.
